DeWitt’s mother’s father’s people were farmers of the Susquehanna.
Nicholas Bucher, born about 1806 and called “a native of Switzerland” in the county history of 1891,
was in Pennsylvania by 1827, when his son Samuel was born in Northampton County.
Swiss and south German emigrants had been taking the same road for more than a century,
drawn by Pennsylvania’s cheap land and its German-speaking Reformed and Lutheran churches.
The Buchers moved up the river to Northumberland County, the farmland of the West Branch around Milton and Watsontown,
where by 1850 they were farming in Chillisquaque Township, and married into long-settled Pennsylvania German families,
the Follmers, Lantzes and Hoys. The Lantzes had been farming in Turbut Township since at least 1810,
and Daniel Follmer, who married Sarah Lantz, farmed there all his life, his land worth $23,000 by 1870;
John Hoy came in 1848 to farm and make brick.
George Benjamin Bucher was born at Chillisquaque in 1862.
His son Harold, born at Watsontown in 1889, went into engineering: Penn State, 1916;
